title: Manetuck
summary: An Islip neck name connected with the 1701 Watchogue sale and an interpretation as a pine or cedar swamp.
address_label: General West Bay Shore / Islip neck area, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point west of Bay Shore, between the Compowams/Bay Shore Brook context and the Islip Watchogue boundary described by Tooker; offset from Compowams for map visibility.
introduction_content: Manetuck is a neck of land in Islip town west of Bay Shore. It is placed in relation to Compowams on the west, Watchogue on the east, and Great South Bay to the south.
translation_content:
Manetuck was first considered as a lookout-place name, but that reading was rejected because the neck did not fit a hilly lookout geography. The preferred interpretation connects it with Delaware words for a pine, spruce, or cedar swamp, supported by the deed's reference to pine trees on the neck.

Why Place Names Matter

“Placenames trigger a mental relationship between the users of the name and the named places.”

— Jan Tent, Placenames as Identity Markers (2017), Placenames Australia, December 2017, PDF page 7
land_loss_content: Manetuck connects deed boundaries, pine swamp ecology, and neighboring Islip placenames. Recording it separately from Compowams and Watchogue helps show how multiple necks and waterways structured the south-shore landscape west of Bay Shore.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general point west of Bay Shore in Islip. It does not mark the exact neck boundary, the historic Watchogue river, or the full Manetuc-Watchogue purchase.
